rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill. It has `---` front matter with `name: habeas`, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`.

The requirement's one obligation is that the description states when to use the skill, in terms of the user's task. The `description` does this. It opens with "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas". It then gives concrete signals: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references. It then states the purpose, which is picking the task skill for design or any change, moves, validation findings, or adoption. It adds that the skill is also the reference for syntax, `habeas status`, `habeas info`, and common gotchas.

The wording is in terms of the work the user is doing, not the skill's internals. The description also names the other bundled skills (`habeas-requirements`, `habeas-refactor`, `habeas-evidence`, `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`). The requirement allows this with MAY, so it is not a gap.

No violation queries are listed, and I found no gap.
